sentences.text: The petitioner is the accused in Crime No. 509 of 2019 of Nagarur Police Station.

The prosecution case as revealed from the FIR is that, on one day in July 2018, at about 9 pm, the accused trespassed into the residence of the defacto complainant and committed rape upon her after threatening her using a knife, taken the naked photos and videos of the defacto complainant and thereafter threatening to publish photos and videos again raped her on another day in July 2018.

Thereafter, he sent those videos and photos to other persons though mobile phone and thereby he alleged to have committed the offences punishable under Section 450,
506(ii) and 376(2)(n) of IPC and Section 67 and 67A of the IT Act.

2. According to the learned Counsel for the petitioner, now the matter has been settled with the defacto complainant and therefore he prayed for quashing all further proceedings against the petitioner.

3. The petition was strongly opposed by the learned Public Prosecutor on the ground that there are serious allegations against the petitioner constituting the offences 2025:KER:84727 alleged against him.

4. As per the allegations in the FI statement on one day during night the petitioner trespassed into the kitchen of the residence of the defacto complainant and committed rape upon her, at knife point,
took her nude photos and videos and thereafter black mailed her using the photos and videos, raped her on another day also.
Thereafter, when she refused to yield to his demand, he sent those photos and videos to others.
The allegations in the FI statement are very serious in nature and the same prima facie discloses the offences alleged against the petitioner.
Since the offences alleged against the petitioner are heinous in nature, the proceedings cannot be quashed for the mere reason that he has settled the dispute with the defacto complainant.
Therefore, I do not find any merits in this Crl.MC and accordingly this Crl.MC is dismissed.

Sd/-
C. PRATHEEP KUMAR JUDGE AKH
